Noah's Giant Roosterfish Catch and Release in San José del Cabo

Fishing Report Jun 27 Written by EXOTIC FISH-CABO

An Unforgettable Encounter with a Giant Roosterfish

Some fishing adventures are remembered for the number of fish caught. Others are defined by a single extraordinary encounter.

For Noah, a morning in June 2026 off the coast of San José del Cabo became one of those unforgettable moments.

Joining Exotic Fish Cabo for a private fishing charter departing from Puerto Los Cabos Marina, Noah headed out to experience the excitement of coastal sportfishing in Baja California Sur.

The goal was to encounter one of the region's most spectacular game fish: the roosterfish.

What happened next exceeded expectations.

An Explosive Strike on Live Mullet

The action began when a large roosterfish spotted the live mullet being presented as bait.

Without warning, the fish exploded at the surface.

Its unmistakable comb-like dorsal fin appeared as it attacked, turning a quiet moment of anticipation into an incredible display of power.

Noah was suddenly connected to an exceptionally large roosterfish.

The battle had begun.

Roosterfish are famous for their aggressive strikes, powerful runs, and remarkable fighting ability. This particular fish demonstrated all three.

As the line tightened, the roosterfish surged away from the boat, forcing Noah to respond quickly.

It was immediately clear that landing this fish would require patience and determination.

A Battle of Strength, Patience, and Determination

The roosterfish fought relentlessly.

Powerful runs, sudden changes of direction, head shakes, and deep dives kept Noah focused throughout the encounter.

Each time he recovered line, the fish seemed ready to challenge him again.

With guidance and assistance from the crew, Noah carefully maintained pressure, adjusting his technique as the battle continued.

It was a demanding fight against one of the most impressive coastal predators found in Los Cabos.

Eventually, after a memorable struggle, Noah brought the giant roosterfish alongside the boat.

Seeing the fish up close was an extraordinary moment.

Its powerful body and distinctive dorsal fin made the encounter even more remarkable.

But the most important part of the adventure was still to come.

A Memorable Catch and a Responsible Release

Rather than keeping such an impressive fish, the crew focused on returning it to the ocean.

The roosterfish was carefully supported alongside the boat and given time to recover before being released.

After the recovery process, the fish was returned to the water.

For Noah, the experience offered something more meaningful than simply landing a trophy-sized fish.

He had faced an exceptional challenge, experienced the remarkable strength of a giant roosterfish, and participated in its release.

Catch-and-release practices are particularly important for roosterfish, a species valued by anglers for its fighting ability and distinctive appearance.

Proper handling, minimizing unnecessary time out of the water, and allowing exhausted fish to recover can help improve their chances after release.

Noah's adventure was a memorable example of how an exciting fishing experience can also include respect for the marine environment.

Trip Highlights

  • Date: June 2026

  • Departure: Puerto Los Cabos Marina, San José del Cabo

  • Angler: Noah

  • Species caught: Roosterfish (Nematistius pectoralis)

  • Bait used: Live mullet

  • Fishing style: Coastal sportfishing

  • Catch highlight: An exceptionally large roosterfish brought alongside the boat

  • Fish handling: Carefully revived and released

  • Experience: Private fishing charter with Exotic Fish Cabo

Why Roosterfish Fishing Is Special in San José del Cabo

Roosterfish are among the most recognizable inshore game fish in the eastern Pacific.

Their spectacular dorsal fins, aggressive surface strikes, and powerful fighting ability make them especially attractive to anglers visiting Baja California Sur.

Unlike marlin and many offshore tuna species, roosterfish are commonly targeted along coastal fishing grounds, where they hunt baitfish such as mullet.

During favorable seasonal conditions, larger roosterfish may move through these productive nearshore areas, offering exciting opportunities for anglers.

Live mullet can be an effective bait, particularly when roosterfish are actively feeding.

However, locating these fish requires attention to baitfish movements, coastal conditions, water temperatures, and changing currents.

The months of May, June, and July are often associated with some of the region's most exciting roosterfish opportunities, although actual activity varies from year to year.

For anglers interested in this species, patience and a flexible approach to fishing locations can make an important difference.

Noah's experience perfectly illustrated the excitement of encountering a powerful roosterfish in its natural environment.

And sometimes, the greatest reward is watching that magnificent fish return to the ocean.

Every fishing trip is different. Weather, currents, water temperature, and seasonal fish activity all influence the opportunities available on any given day.

Catches are never guaranteed.
